title: Ivo and the Parish
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Parish, founder of the seaside town of Vesper's Hollow, is exhumed for a land dispute, hotel concierge Coral Marchetti discovers it empty — and realizes the 'closed' death from thirty years ago was staged. Using their concierge's gift for reading people and patterns, Coral uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families, who faked Parish's death to hide that he was dying of poison — poisoned by his own heirs. The trail leads to Coral's found family at the Hotel Meridian, where the kindly night manager, Odette, is revealed to be Parish's unacknowledged daughter who swapped the body to protect her mother's name. In the end, Coral must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the family they've built, resolving it by forcing a public confession that destroys the heirs' power but spares Odette, who leaves town — leaving Coral with justice won and love lost.
about_author: W. M. Delacroix spent a decade working front desks in small coastal hotels before turning to fiction, collecting the confessions strangers make to concierges at 2 a.m. They write mysteries about people who notice too much, from a house with an unreliable view of the sea.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Talk
chapters.summary: Coral Marchetti's POV. A day in the life of the Hotel Meridian's concierge: Coral reads guests like weather, defuses a feuding couple, and shares late tea with night manager Odette Bram, the closest thing to family they have. The beat is warmth laced with loneliness — Coral notices everything but belongs nowhere.

chapters.title: An Order of Shovels
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Surveyors arrive asking odd questions about the old Parish plot on the headland; a land dispute requires exhuming town founder Aldous Parish, dead thirty years. Coral books rooms for the exhumation crew and notes one guest lying about her name. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gave Back
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the exhumation, the coffin is opened before the whole stunned town: it holds sandbags and a stranger's shoes. Coral watches the founding families' faces and catches the youngest heir, Marcus Vale, looking not shocked but afraid. Beat: the closed past cracks open.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Condolences
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral digs into the archive of the funeral week — guest registers, floral orders, a hotel ledger from 1994 — and finds a room booked under a name that matches no mourner. Sheriff Ilsa Reyes warns them off. Beat: curiosity hardening into compulsion.

chapters.title: The Heirs of Aldous Parish
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Marcus Vale POVs. Coral attends the memorial the Vales throw to control the narrative; Marcus privately burns a letter he shouldn't have kept. Coral clocks the burn smell. Beat: the reader learns the heirs are hiding something specific while Coral only senses smoke.

chapters.title: Odette's Long Shift
chapters.summary: Odette Bram's POV, first time. Odette works the night desk, restless, checking the door every time it opens. She visits the cemetery after hours and stands over the empty grave. Her interiority hints at a personal stake she refuses to name. Beat: dread and tenderness entwined.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following the money: Parish's will left everything to a trust controlled by the founding families, but Coral finds a monthly payment made for decades to an unnamed recipient — hush money shaped like charity. Beat: the mystery gains a spine.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't a Guest
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confronts the misnamed guest from chapter two: a private investigator hired by Marcus to find out if anyone else knows the coffin was light. Coral plays dumb, then follows her. Beat: Coral shifts from observer to player.

chapters.title: Salt and Arsenic
chapters.summary: Sheriff Reyes's POV. The state lab reports traces consistent with arsenic on the coffin lining — meaning Parish may have been poisoned, and someone knew enough to fake the burial fast. Reyes reopens the case against the town's wishes. Beat: stakes turn criminal and mortal.

chapters.title: The Founding Families' Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Catering the annual founders' dinner, Coral serves the four dynasty heads and listens: each blames another for the exhumation disaster. One matriarch, Evelyn Vale, quietly threatens Coral's job. Beat: power shows its teeth; Coral refuses to flinch.

chapters.title: What Odette Kept
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Flashback to 1994: young Odette and her mother, Parish's housekeeper, receiving word of his death — and his instruction that mother and child be erased from all records. Odette reveals to the reader (not Coral) that she took something from the house the night before the funeral. Beat: sympathy deepens, suspicion blooms.

chapters.title: The Empty Room 312
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cross-referencing the 1994 ledger, Coral proves Room 312 was occupied during the funeral week by someone arriving before the death was announced — impossible unless the death was expected. The signature is smudged, but the handwriting feels familiar. Beat: the noose tightens around someone Coral loves.

chapters.title: Threats at the Front Desk
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Escalation: Coral's tires are slashed, then a dead gull on the doorstep with a note — stop digging. Odette insists Coral move into the hotel's staff quarters 'for safety.' Beat: fear, and the first open tenderness between Coral and Odette.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Marcus Vale's POV. Cornered by his grandmother Evelyn, Marcus admits he hired the investigator; she reveals the family has known the coffin was empty for thirty years and paid to keep it so. Marcus, disgusted, anonymously slips Coral the trust's real accounting. Beat: the conspiracy turns on itself.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With Marcus's documents, Coral reconstructs the truth: Parish was slowly poisoned by the heirs to seize the trust early; the loyal housekeeper helped him stage his death to escape and expose them — but he died anyway, weeks later, far away. Beat: grief for a man Coral never met, fury at those who knew.

chapters.title: Where Aldous Parish Actually Lies
chapters.summary: Coral and Odette's shared scene. Following the payments, they find an unmarked grave upcoast — Parish's true resting place, tended for decades by someone who left fresh flowers. Odette's composure finally cracks. Beat: intimacy and revelation on the edge of confession.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on Room 312
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Alone with the old ledger, Coral matches the smudged signature to the night-shift logbook: Odette's mother checked in that week — and Odette countersigned. Coral realizes the person they love most orchestrated the empty coffin. Beat: betrayal and understanding arriving together.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. On the flats at dawn, Odette tells Coral everything: her mother helped Parish vanish to shield them both; when he died, Odette swapped the coffin herself at nineteen, alone, terrified. She asks Coral not to hand her to the town. Beat: love laid bare against duty.

chapters.title: The Town That Buried a Lie
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The founding families move to declare the exhumation a clerical error and seal the records forever, buying the sheriff's superiors. Coral realizes silence is being purchased at scale — and that Odette's secret is their only leverage. Beat: the moral trap closes.

chapters.title: Everything Coral Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax begins: at a packed town hall vote to seal the records, Coral takes the floor and lays out the poisoning, the trust theft, and the payments — naming the heirs, withholding Odette's name. Chaos erupts; Evelyn Vale accuses Coral of fabrication. Beat: courage as performance under fire.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Vesper's Hollow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Marcus corroborates Coral publicly with the documents; Evelyn is arrested for the poisoning; the trust dissolves. Reyes suspects there was an accomplice in 1994 but lets the trail go cold, meeting Coral's eyes across the room. Beat: justice done, imperfectly, deliberately.

chapters.title: Checkout Time
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Odette, freed but unable to stay in a town that nearly consumed her, resigns and leaves on the morning bus; she and Coral part with an unfinished promise. Coral stays — keeper of the Meridian, of the town's true story, of a found family smaller now but still theirs. Beat: bittersweet resolution; love against duty, duty chosen, love remembered.
